key_insight: Zero-shot large language models extracted colorectal cancer symptoms from discharge notes more accurately than rule-based and NER pipelines, with Gemini 3.5 Flash performing best overall.
clinical_relevance: This approach could speed scalable symptom surveillance from routine oncology notes and reduce reliance on manual chart review or institution-specific NLP rules.
method: Analyzed 2,704 MIMIC-IV colorectal cancer discharge notes.
Built a 46-symptom target list from validated symptom instruments.
Compared rule-based matching, clinical NER, zero-shot Claude/Gemini, and hybrid negation-filtered variants against adjudicated ground truth.
evidence_signal: On a 200-note gold standard with dual-rater adjudication, Gemini 3.5 Flash achieved Macro F1 0.70 and Micro F1 0.86, outperforming rule-based (Macro F1 0.44) and NER (Macro F1 0.38) methods.
watch_item: Post-hoc negation filtering reduced LLM performance, suggesting negation handling needs syntactic scope validation rather than fixed-window rules.
paper_title: Leveraging Large Language Models for Colorectal Cancer Symptom Extraction from MIMIC-IV Clinical Notes
